clue.text: Shout at new arrival, who is tearful

parts.note: to shout is to cry out
a newborn baby is the family's new arrival

explanation.surface: Someone yells at a newborn, and the infant starts weeping.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a description, 'one who is tearful', that stands in for the noun; 'at' only joins the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A person given to weeping easily is mockingly called this, so the phrase describes one.

clue.text: Hermit and half the rest having different clues

indicators.note: only the first half of the word rest is taken, its opening two letters

parts.note: the word rest is written in the clue

indicators.note: different signals that the letters of clues are put in another order

explanation.surface: A hermit, together with half the remaining people, has been given varying hints.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' keeps RE from REST, and 'different' turns CLUES into CLUSE.
explanation.definitionFit: A hermit lives alone, apart from society, which is exactly what a recluse does.

clue.text: Intrude and nearly get where the drinks are

parts.note: drinks are served at the bar of a pub

indicators.note: nearly means the word is cut short by its final letter

explanation.surface: Someone tries to push in and almost reaches the bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly' drops the T of GET to leave GE.
explanation.definitionFit: To barge in is to burst in rudely, so the verb alone serves as a synonym for intrude.

clue.text: Warm when dry, cool when wet

definitions.text: Warm when dry, cool when wet

parts.words: Warm when dry, cool when wet
parts.note: a dry bedcover keeps you warm, while the idiom for a killjoy who cools everyone's spirits makes the same item soggy

explanation.surface: A riddle about something whose effect changes with moisture.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'wet' half rests on the idiom 'a wet blanket', someone who dampens others' fun.
explanation.definitionFit: A bedcover warms when dry, and the idiomatic wet version describes a spoilsport who cools enthusiasm.

clue.text: United and lusted after her first

indicators.note: first tells us to take only the opening letter of her

parts.note: to itch for something is to crave it

explanation.surface: Two people were joined, and one had desired the woman first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'her first' gives H, which leads the charade.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting hitched is informal for getting married, so the participle means joined or wed.

clue.text: Make prisoner bury nothing at first

parts.note: to inter is to bury a body

indicators.note: at first means only the initial letter of nothing is wanted

explanation.surface: An instruction to lock someone up and bury nothing at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at first' takes N from 'nothing'.
explanation.definitionFit: To intern is to confine someone, especially in wartime, so it means to make a prisoner of them.

clue.text: Sweet Chanel departed, hot inside

indicators.note: inside means one letter is placed within the designer's first name

parts.note: Coco Chanel was the French fashion designer
H is the abbreviation for hot on taps
late means dead, departed

explanation.surface: The late, glamorous Chanel had a hot interior.
explanation.walkthrough: Coco Chanel was the famous French couturier; 'inside' places the hot abbreviation after her name's first letter, and 'departed' means dead, as in 'the late'.
explanation.definitionFit: A chocolate is a piece of confectionery, which in Britain is called a sweet.

clue.text: Epistle he's sent us from ancient Greek city

parts.note: Ep. is the standard abbreviation for epistle
the apostrophe drops, leaving the three letters

explanation.surface: A New Testament letter is sent to us from an old Greek city.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface nods to St Paul's Epistle to the Ephesians; 'sent' and 'from' only link.
explanation.definitionFit: This was an ancient Greek city in Asia Minor, home of the Temple of Artemis.

clue.text: Prophet in return fell with toe broken

indicators.note: broken means the letters of the three words are smashed and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A seer took a tumble on the way back and broke a toe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' rearranges RETURN, FELL and TOE; 'in' and 'with' only link.
explanation.definitionFit: A fortune teller claims to predict the future, as a prophet does.

clue.text: Damage at the front of sports jalopy

indicators.note: at the front of means the initial letter of sports is taken

parts.note: a jalopy is an old battered car

explanation.surface: Damage visible on the front of a sporty old banger.
explanation.definitionFit: A scar is a mark of damage, and to scar is to damage permanently.

clue.text: Sign made by pastor with hope

indicators.note: made signals that something new is formed from the letters of pastor and hope

explanation.surface: A gesture made by a clergyman who is hopeful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made' rearranges PASTOR and HOPE together; 'by' and 'with' only link.
explanation.definitionFit: The apostrophe is a punctuation mark, a written sign.

clue.text: Be in luck in north Germany

indicators.note: in means the word Be goes inside the word luck

explanation.surface: A wish that someone has good fortune in the north of Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal. The definition is loose: the answer is a Baltic port city in north Germany, not the region itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Lübeck is a Hanseatic port city on the Baltic in northern Germany, so it stands for a place there.

clue.text: Slowcoach tries too awkwardly

indicators.note: awkwardly means the letters of tries and too are clumsily jumbled

explanation.surface: A sluggish person makes clumsy attempts as well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awkwardly' rearranges TRIES and TOO together.
explanation.definitionFit: The tortoise is proverbially slow, as in the fable with the hare, so it is a slowcoach.

clue.text: Silly berk with love nest by the way

indicators.note: silly signals the letters are rearranged foolishly

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, written as O

explanation.surface: A foolish idiot with a romantic hideaway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Silly' rearranges BERK, O and NEST. A berk is British slang for a fool. 'by the way' looks like a phrase meaning 'incidentally'.
explanation.definitionFit: A kerbstone edges the pavement beside the road, literally lying by the way.

clue.text: Animal makes robber suppress a cry of shock

indicators.note: suppress means the robber holds down the cry, which sits inside

parts.note: a bandit is a robber
coo is a British exclamation of surprise

explanation.surface: A creature causes a thief to stifle a gasp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suppress' is the container signal: the robber holds the cry down inside, before his final letter. 'Coo!' is a dated British exclamation of surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandicoot is a small Australian marsupial, so it is an animal.

clue.text: Flower girl is seen in time

indicators.note: seen in means the word is appears within the time word

parts.note: a day is a period of time

explanation.surface: A bridesmaid carrying flowers turns up on schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen in' is the container signal. 'Flower girl' reads as a bridesmaid but is a girl named after a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: Daisy is both a common flower and a girl's name, so it is a girl bearing a flower name.

clue.text: Intimidate daughter and uncle's wife

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter in genealogies
an uncle's wife is an aunt

explanation.surface: A daughter and her aunt by marriage frighten someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To daunt someone is to make them afraid or discouraged, to intimidate them.

clue.text: Unsaintly staff — talented and friendly

indicators.note: unsaintly means the abbreviation for saint is removed from the word staff

parts.note: able means skilled, talented

explanation.surface: Workers who are no saints but are clever and pleasant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unsaintly' removes ST (saint) from STAFF, leaving AFF.
explanation.definitionFit: An affable person is good-natured and easy to talk to, which is friendly.

clue.text: Tiger cats can be cunning

indicators.note: can be signals the letters of Tiger and cats may be turned into something else

explanation.surface: Big cats such as tigers can be crafty hunters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can be' rearranges TIGER and CATS together.
explanation.definitionFit: Strategic means carefully planned for advantage, which here is stretched to shrewd or cunning.

clue.text: Pain-reliever for girl infusing all of body except the head

indicators.note: infusing means one piece is poured into the girl's name

parts.note: Anne is a girl's name

indicators.note: except the head means the first letter of body is dropped

explanation.surface: A painkiller for a woman that spreads through her whole body but not her head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'except the head' drops the first letter of the body word, and 'infusing' pours what is left into the girl's name; 'all of' only adds to the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: An anodyne is a medicine that relieves pain, a painkiller.

clue.text: One of us is desirin' another!

indicators.note: another means the word is rearranged into a different word

explanation.surface: A colloquial remark that someone in the group fancies someone else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' rearranges DESIRIN; 'is' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: An insider is a member of the group, someone who is one of us.

clue.text: Shape of guru half-visible in flames

indicators.note: in means one piece goes inside the word for flames

parts.note: flames make a fire

indicators.note: half-visible means only the first half of guru can be seen

explanation.surface: The form of a mystic, partly seen through a blaze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-visible' keeps GU from GURU, which goes 'in' FIRE.
explanation.definitionFit: A figure is an outline or form, which is a shape.

clue.text: Authorised chemical company to get into animal food

indicators.note: to get into means the company goes inside the food

parts.note: offal is the entrails of an animal used as food
ICI was Imperial Chemical Industries, a big British chemical company

explanation.surface: An approved firm is getting into the pet food business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get into' is the container signal; ICI, Imperial Chemical Industries, was once Britain's biggest chemical firm.
explanation.definitionFit: Something official has authority behind it, so it is authorised.

clue.text: Clumsy when giving ring to a fish

parts.note: a ring is round, like the letter O
taken as written; that the letters also run on from 'to a fish' is a coincidence, as the clue builds them from ring plus a fish

explanation.surface: Being ungainly while handing a ring over to a fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'giving ... to' sets O in front of A FISH; 'when' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Oafish means like an oaf, a lumbering lout, so it is clumsy.

clue.text: Undisguised conqueror of old

definitions.meaning: a member of the Germanic people who conquered Gaul in the early Middle Ages

explanation.definitionFit: Frank means openly honest, and the Franks were the ancient people who conquered Gaul, giving France its name.

clue.text: Downright dead!

definitions.meaning: used as an intensifier, as in dead right, meaning totally

explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means completely, like downright, and the colloquial intensifier dead (dead certain) has the same sense.

clue.text: Boy's a trifle bandy-legged

indicators.note: a trifle means only part of the word is taken, a run of letters within it

explanation.surface: A lad is slightly bow-legged.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit inside 'bandy'; ''s' stands for 'is' and only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Andy is a boy's name, short for Andrew.

clue.text: Down with her earlier act!

indicators.note: earlier means the act comes before the word her

parts.note: a feat is a deed or act

explanation.surface: A condemnation of a woman's earlier behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Down' reads as a cry of 'down with', but it is the soft plumage; 'earlier' says the act comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Down is the fine soft plumage of birds, made of small feathers.

clue.text: Mugs of schoolmasters catching an unfinished piece of history

indicators.note: catching means the schoolmasters hold another piece inside

parts.note: beak is British school slang for a schoolmaster

indicators.note: unfinished means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: an era is a period of history

explanation.surface: The faces of teachers caught up in a fragment of history lesson.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfinished' drops the last letter of the period of history, and 'catching' sets what remains inside the teachers, before their final letter. Beak is old British school slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Beakers are drinking cups, so they are mugs.
